summary: Phase 149O.20L.7L.2 -- HMIC-001 v1.4 Consumer-Status and Dependency-Header Repair Independent Verification. FINAL VERDICT: NOT VERIFIED -- CONTRACT REPAIR INCOMPLETE. Independently reconstructed F-7L-1 from production source, not from 149O.20L.7L.1's prose: import at hatp_mandatory_cutover.py:74, call at line 952 inside _assess_hatp_mandatory_activation_readiness_at_root, eighth of eight readiness checks, re-invoked lock-held immediately before any real HATP_MANDATORY activation write, sole production consumer confirmed by repository-wide grep, certification independence confirmed. Independently re-derived the chronology via git log --oneline (149O.20L.3's wiring commit e2ccb7a3 sits between 149O.20K's and 149O.20L.7K's own commits). F-7L-1: CLOSED. F-7L-2 independently confirmed: HBDC-001's own Version header reads 1.1; derive_contract_versions executed live returns HBDC-001=1.1, matching the repaired Depends-on header exactly; precedent (section 54/section 52) applies a fortiori. F-7L-2: CLOSED. HMIC-REQ-052's normative membership test independently confirmed byte-unchanged -- only descriptive prose was corrected; no normative weakening. HMIC-REQ-050's 30-file enumeration independently re-extracted from the live contract and diffed programmatically, entry-for-entry, against production's _FROZEN_SRC_PCAE_RELATIVE_FILES + _FROZEN_REPOSITORY_ROOT_RELATIVE_FILES: zero divergence. implementation_scope_digest independently recomputed live (65ff8ab06b5cd7feb2505742cfbb112ffd386c5b2cf34c2d7f3446d92afe15b8) and at a disposable pre-repair worktree (95cfd008): identical both times. Seven named production/contract files git-hash-object compared against the pre-repair baseline: all seven byte-identical. Same-version repair policy verdict: SAME-VERSION REPAIR VALID. HMIC version identity confirmed v1.4 throughout, no mixed-version state. However, independently re-adjudicating F-7L-5 without inheriting 149O.20L.7L.1's own labels revealed that its deferral of attack-matrix rows 33/34/36/37 does not hold up: each row's live, present-tense 'production still computes the N-file/M-member set' claim is directly, trivially false against today's production constants (30 files, 5 contract-version members, both independently confirmed above) -- establishing this required no 'wide architecture interpretation', only reading the current production constants, contradicting 149O.20L.7L.1's own stated deferral rationale. Row 34 additionally falsely claims a hard-coded False ceiling and zero readiness/cutover callers for the certification validator; independently falsified by direct source reading (hatp_mandatory_cutover.py:876-899 computes this term live via the validator; the validator's own Step 9, hatp_mandatory_certification.py:2038-2053, freshly recomputes and compares implementation_scope_digest as part of a live readiness gate) and by git log chronology (the wiring, Phase 149O.19.5F, independently confirmed more recent than 149O.19.5E.1's own commit, i.e. it predates and falsifies row 34's text, by roughly a hundred phases -- the identical defect class F-7L-1 itself found, undiscovered by 149O.20L.7L.1's own scan). Row 38 independently confirmed correctly repaired. Separately, adversarial construction against the F-7L-7 guard tightening (literal ast.parse calls against constructed adversarial import snippets, not inherited from any prior phase's claim) found a real, reproducible, pre-existing gap: the AST-level import guard (test_no_module_under_src_pcae_imports_the_producer_at_ast_level) only records ImportFrom.module, never .names, so `from pcae.core import hatp_deployment_binding_admin` (a standard Python submodule-import idiom) evades it entirely; the multi-line parenthesized form of the same idiom additionally evades the tightened textual guards in the one exempted file (hatp_mandatory_certification.py), directly contradicting 149O.20L.7L.1's own section 56.10 completeness claim. This gap predates 149O.20L.7L.1 (the helper is untouched by its diff) and does not affect F-7L-1/F-7L-2's own closure. Regression evidence: targeted 6-file selection A/B'd against a disposable pre-repair worktree, zero new failures, one resolved (matching the header fix). Full raw -m fast_green suite run twice in parallel (HEAD and pre-repair worktree): 262 vs 263 unique FAILED/ERROR node IDs, comm-diffed, zero new failures, exactly one resolved -- this raw count is far larger than 149O.20L.7L.1's own report characterized (it used an unlisted deselect set), but the underlying zero-regression property is independently confirmed, on stronger evidence (full node-ID diff, not a curated deselect list). Deselected clean re-run using the full independently-derived 262-item deselect list: 7552 passed, 0 failed, 5 skipped, confirmed twice (one order-dependent flake in test_shell_gate.py reproduced as passing in isolation on the second confirmation run, matching 149O.20L.7L.1's own documented backend_cli/shell_gate flakiness pattern). New 16-test regression module added, all passing, documenting both new findings as guards expected to flip once a future narrow repair lands. No Dell access, no RepositoryIdentity, no DeploymentBinding, no election, no CHGR, no certification, no Boundary C/A work -- confirmed by repository-wide find and by this phase's own command history. 7J section 31 source-scope finding: remains NOT CLOSED (this verification is not clean). Recommended next phase: 149O.20L.7L.3, a narrow, same-version, contract-text-and-test-only repair of rows 33/34/36/37 and the _pcae_imports AST-guard gap, followed by re-verification, before the 7J finding may close or first-use sequencing architecture may begin. HATP production remains NOT READY. Runtime remains Observed / observe / unavailable.
